name: Abu Firas al-Hamdani
bio: Abu Firas al-Harith ibn Sa'id ibn Hamdan was born in 320 AH (932 CE), a cousin of Sayf al-Dawla, the Hamdanid prince of Aleppo, who loved and honoured him, took him on his campaigns and made him governor of Manbij and Harran. Wounded in a battle with the Byzantines, he was taken prisoner in 351 AH (962 CE) and held in Constantinople for several years until Sayf al-Dawla ransomed him for a great sum; the poems he wrote in captivity are known as the Rumiyyat, the Byzantine poems. The vizier al-Sahib ibn Abbad used to say that poetry began with a king and ended with a king, meaning Imru' al-Qays and Abu Firas. He was killed in 357 AH (968 CE) at Sadad near Homs, according to Ibn Khallikan, by a follower of Sa'd al-Dawla, Sayf al-Dawla's son, whose maternal uncle and rival he was.
